newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kim's speech seen to little impact shares.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kim's speech seen to little impact shares.

text.p: President Kim Young-sam's address to the nation on Tuesday morning is not expected to contain any major new economic measures that would shake the bourse out of its current slump, brokers said.
Hopes that the address would include an early expansion of the foreign shareholding ceiling had supported buying interest last week, but this expectation has since waned, they said.
"I think the speech will be very much political and don't think there will be any spectacular economic issues in it," said Choe Seung-wook of Schroders Securities.
The index closed Monday at 676.59, down 4.65 points.
Brokers said that if Kim made a strong political move to end the Hanbo Steel loan scandal, that may have a short-term market boosting effect.
But other negative factors, such as high interest rates and worries the central bank would tighten the money supply, would limit strong rises.
Brokers said semiconductor makers could rebound after Merrill Lynch recommended U.S. memory chip stocks Micron Technology and Texas Instruments.
Merrill Lynch said in a report that unit demand for PCs remained strong. -- KATHERINE BRUCE (822) 727 5644
